title: Observed and shuffled burst fractions correlated at 0.958 across 27 IBL thalamic nuclei
abstract: We tested which part of regional burst fraction depends on interval order. We reused signed IBL Brain-Wide Map summaries for 9,941 units from 97 mice in 27 thalamic nuclei. Observed and interval-shuffled nucleus fractions had Spearman correlation 0.958 (mouse bootstrap interval 0.902 to 0.982). The mean excess was 0.075 percentage points, with an interval of -0.113 to 0.257. Subtraction left 12.6% of the across-nucleus variance. The excess retained structure across separate mouse groups, so a small grand mean did not imply no order effect. We derived finite-permutation means and variances for burst spike and event counts. All formulas passed exhaustive checks on 88,573 interval-category sequences. A two-state renewal simulation showed that a global shuffle can give negative excess from rate changes alone. Saved biological tables lack the interval counts needed to apply the exact method, so empirical results use the original 20-shuffle estimates. No wiring specificity or calcium mechanism is established. Code, proof, input hashes, input tables, draws and figures support reproduction.

display.caption: Observed and shuffled regional fractions, excess with mouse intervals, and cross-half mouse rank correlations. Intervals condition on all 27 nuclei being present.
Exact burst-spike expectation and a constructed two-state renewal control. The control tests the exchangeability assumption; it does not estimate rate-state effects in IBL.
